solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Facial expression with a twist in it

definitions.text: Facial expression with a twist in it

indicators.note: a twist inside the word means two of its inner letters swap places

parts.note: a smile showing the teeth, the commonest facial expression in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a wry, crooked face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a twist in it' moves the R of GRIN past the I. The whole clue is also the definition: a girn is a grin twisted into a grotesque face.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern British and Scots word for a snarl or grotesque grimace, literally a contorted smile.

clue.text: Say which arrangement of Beethoven's last piano overture includes cello in the middle

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks material, so the following letters are reordered
only the central letter of the instrument's name is used
the final letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: A musical note about a piano arrangement of a Beethoven piece with a cello part added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' rearranges N (Beethoven's last), PIANO, OVERTURE and L (the middle of cello). 'Say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, 'which' introduces a clause referring back to a noun, so it is an instance of this word class.

clue.text: Zoo attraction? Polar bears might exert such a pull

definitions.meaning: punningly, the pull of creatures at a zoo

definitions.text: Polar bears might exert such a pull
definitions.meaning: bears living at the poles, like magnets, would draw things toward them

explanation.surface: Visitors flock to see polar bears, whose charisma draws the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are puns: one reads the phrase as charm belonging to beasts, the other reads 'Polar' as magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means personal charisma, but literally suggests a creature's magnetic force, as at a zoo or at the poles.

clue.text: Setter tries in the same place again

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to bid is to make an attempt, so the setter tries means I bid

explanation.surface: The compiler has another go at the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in references to mean a source already cited, in the same work.

clue.text: Fix up advance rent by day and date

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the loan word is split by the day

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

explanation.surface: Someone arranges to pay rent early, on a particular day and date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but means torn: 'rent by' splits the loan word around the day. 'up' reverses the word for fix, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A date can be a person one is going out with romantically, here a female partner.

clue.text: Wrongly thought to equal 1 mile?

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, going wrong or awry
the proverb says a near miss is as good as a mile

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly believes a distance is a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition relies on the proverb 'a miss is as good as a mile': a narrow failure is still a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes awry is done wrongly, out of order or faulty.

clue.text: Establish in rear property

indicators.note: the word for establish sits inside the word for rear

parts.note: the American word for a backside
to set something up is to establish it

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a business in the back premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things owned, the holdings or possessions that count as one's property.

clue.text: Problem outside restaurant for rock band

indicators.note: the arithmetic problem surrounds the eatery

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: A musical group has trouble outside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock band' reads as a group of musicians, but it is a layer of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology this is a bed or layer of rock lying between others.

clue.text: Entitling one to return, if note is retained, jewellery

indicators.note: the note letter is held within the reversed number word
the word one is to be read backwards

parts.note: bling is slang for showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Wearing flashy jewellery gives someone a title, provided a banknote is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the number word, making ENO, and 'is retained' keeps the note letter within it, giving ENNO.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the nobility is to give them a title, so the participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Guard's folly, regularly missing provocative pest

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, keeping the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A guard's foolish mistake lets in an irritating nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting horsefly, and figuratively a person who annoys others into action, a provoking irritant.

clue.text: Performed revolutionary tune that's found in Spanish bars

parts.note: to have sung is to have performed, here sang

indicators.note: turning round means the word is reversed

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A rebel song is sung in Spanish taverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish wine punch with fruit, served in bars across Spain.

clue.text: Got involved, and won prize in audition

indicators.note: in hearing, the words are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: being awarded a medal means you won a prize

explanation.surface: A performer got a part and won a prize at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' signals a sound-alike: MEDALLED sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in others' affairs is to get involved where one is not wanted.

clue.text: Tests rate limits under duress

indicators.note: letters forced under pressure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Speed limits are tested under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under duress' rearranges RATE LIMITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Races against the clock, as in cycling, are trials or tests of speed.

clue.text: Musical West End girl's self-description pre-elocution lessons?

definitions.meaning: a stage show with songs, here the Lerner and Loewe one based on Pygmalion

definitions.text: West End girl's self-description pre-elocution lessons?
definitions.meaning: a Mayfair lady, said in a Cockney accent before lessons, comes out with these sounds

explanation.surface: A London girl describes herself before learning to speak properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a smart district of London's West End; spoken in Eliza Doolittle's Cockney, 'Mayfair lady' becomes the show's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 musical about Eliza Doolittle, a Cockney flower seller taught to speak like a lady.

clue.text: Unwritten rule in backward Southeast Asian language

indicators.note: the letter for rule goes inside the reversed language
the language name is reversed

parts.note: Lao is the language of Laos
R is short for rule, as in rex

explanation.surface: An unwritten convention exists in a language of Southeast Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns LAO into OAL; R goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, as in an oral tradition.

clue.text: 20's heavy rock noise ultimately holds nothing for attractive woman

parts.note: 20 across is Iron Maiden; iron is the chemical symbol Fe
the second word, maiden, gives M, the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the music and final letter surround the word for nothing

parts.note: heavy metal is a hard rock genre, shortened to metal
sweet FA, Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: the last letter of the word noise is taken

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band's racket holds nothing for a glamorous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to the band at 20 across: its two words, iron and maiden, each give a short abbreviation. 'ultimately' takes noise's last letter, and 'holds' makes MEFATALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who lures men to their downfall, a dangerously alluring figure.

clue.text: A woman may sound in a state

indicators.note: these words said aloud give the answer

parts.note: a woman is a lass, and may is can, giving a lass can

explanation.surface: A woman can make a noise when she is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like 'agitated', but it means belonging to a US state. 'A lass can', said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or from America's largest state, in its far northwest, so it describes something found in a state.

clue.text: Run off with ball between posts?

indicators.note: the two letters go between the posts, inside the word for them

parts.note: the goal is formed by the goalposts
O is a round letter shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: A footballer scores by running the ball between the posts.
explanation.walkthrough: AWOL means absent without leave; W and O go 'between' GOA and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert, leaving without permission, is to run off.

clue.text: I am one broken by loss of purpose

indicators.note: the phrase is broken up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone says they are broken by losing their sense of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges I AM ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociological term for the breakdown of social norms and the resulting aimlessness in a person.

clue.text: Leave out overheard appeal to Romney

indicators.note: what is overheard is heard, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: Mitt Romney is a US politician; an appeal to him is O Mitt

explanation.surface: Someone is caught making a plea to the US politician Mitt Romney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overheard' signals a sound-alike: 'O, Mitt!' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip or exclude something is to leave it out.

clue.text: Presswoman in a suit, very sharp underneath the surface

definitions.meaning: punningly, a woman who presses, a press being a smoothing iron and a woman a maiden

definitions.text: in a suit, very sharp underneath the surface
definitions.meaning: a human-shaped case whose inner surface bristles with spikes

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted female journalist hides her edge beneath a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits as press plus woman; the second describes the medieval torture device.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary torture cabinet in human form, lined with spikes that pierce the occupant.

clue.text: Female left fellow inside — he may be affected by the moon

definitions.text: he may be affected by the moon

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for female

parts.note: a woman is a female person

explanation.surface: A woman leaves a man indoors, and he is affected by the full moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary man who turns into a wolf at the full moon, the werewolf of horror films.

clue.text: Setter and moose, left out among inheritors of the earth?

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: the elk is the European name for the moose

explanation.surface: The setter and a moose, overlooked, hope to inherit the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible says the meek shall inherit the earth; 'out' removes L from ELK, leaving EK.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's Sermon on the Mount promises the earth to the humble and gentle, so the definition names one of them.

clue.text: Fire's said to follow this and make it a mess

indicators.note: making a mess of the letters means jumbling them

explanation.surface: A fire is said to follow, making a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the drill command 'ready, aim, fire'; 'mess' rearranges MAKE IT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Before firing, a shooter points the weapon at the target; the order is ready, aim, fire.

clue.text: Summit of Asia-Pacific forum's talked about

indicators.note: what is talked about is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: APEC is the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum

explanation.surface: A summit of an Asia-Pacific forum is much discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a summit meeting, which suits APEC, but it means the highest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something, the top of a mountain.

clue.text: More than one helping in duel falls injured

indicators.note: letters that are injured are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: More than one person is hurt when a duellist falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges DUEL FALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Several servings scooped with a big spoon are helpings.

clue.text: Withdraw article in German about English member of different generation

indicators.note: drawing back means reading the article backwards

parts.note: ein is the German indefinite article
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws a German article about the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' turns EIN into NIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's daughter belongs to the generation below, a relative one step down the family tree.
